ai.description: The South Andaman Krait is a slender, medium-sized snake reaching 1 meter. It is glossy black with narrow, white crossbands and a distinct, rounded snout. The subcaudal scales are entirely undivided.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Bungarus andamanensis* is distinguished by its unique pattern of narrow, white crossbands on a dark body that often break into spots, unlike the distinct, complete rings of other Indian kraits.
ai.habitat: *Bungarus andamanensis* inhabits the tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of the South Andaman Islands, typically found at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The South Andaman Krait is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dark to actively forage for other snakes and small vertebrates across the forest floor.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Bungarus andamanensis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–10 eggs. While specific breeding data is limited, nesting typically occurs during the monsoon season in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Bungarus andamanensis* is endemic to the Andaman Islands in the Bay of Bengal, where it is primarily found in lowland tropical forests and near human settlements.
